verdict: Claude Haiku 5.5 is a good place to start for classifying sections. The Strands Decider 2B comes close if you give each class a one-line description of what its pages look like and send it the first two page images. It then gave the right class to 95% of correctly split sections, against 98% for Claude Haiku 5.5 with the same descriptions, at about the same cost ($31 per 1,000 packets). With the preset's longer class descriptions, written for an LLM, it got 77%. Both got about the same share of sections exactly right (77% and 78%), because most errors come from finding where each section starts, which Claude Haiku 5.5 does in every row. Test it on your own packets.
